newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hokuriku Electric to buy Indonesian coal.
newsitem.headline: Hokuriku Electric to buy Indonesian coal.

text.p: Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc said on Wednesday that it had agreed to purchase an annual 120,000 tonnes of coal from Indonesia's P.T. Adaro Indonesia between 1998 and 2001.
A Hokuriku spokesman said he believed it was the first time for a Japanese power utility to conclude a long-term contract with the Indonesian company.
The spokesman declined to provide details on the terms of the agreement.

He said the Indonesian coal would be used at two 500,000-kilowatt (kw) power plants, one operating in Ishikawa prefecture and another in Fukui prefecture, both in central Japan on the Sea of Japan coast.
Hokuriku Electric also plans to start operation of two coal-fired thermal power plants, both with capacity of 700,000 kw, in 1998 and 2000.
"We decided to conclude this agreement because of our plans for new coal-fired thermal power plants," the spokesman said.
